title: plotly_chart using cached data on axis
body:
### Checklist - [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary I've described the error on [streamlit forum](https:///t/plotly-chart-displays-index-names-that-do-not-exists/35273). The issue is that plotly_chart function appears to have a cached data problem, since the function plot names on the y-axis that are not in plotly figure (anymore). I tested this issue using either the plotly Figure object and the figure json. The json does not have this data saved (if you plot the figure on another page, i works as it should). ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python I cannot provide my code here. The json I'm using is: { "data": [ { "marker": { "color": "#1D57A5" }, "orientation": "h", "showlegend": false, "x": [ 120.1380999999999, 106.06296666666667, 315.50575, 60.151150000000015, 1.4062199999999963, 93.94610000000003, 40.326899999999995, -248.98569999999995, -57.8537 ], "y": [ "axistitle1", "axistitle2", "axistitle3", "axistitle4", "axistitle5", "axistitle6", "axistitle7", "axistitle8", "axistitle9" ], "type": "bar" } ], "layout": { "template": { "layout": { "colorway": [ "#1D57A5", "#00B5E2", "#b8b6b6", "#e30b0b", "#141414", " #fca605", "#0ac200", "#4285F4", "#A6771E", "#F4B400", "#0F9D58", "#185ABC", "#B31412", "#EA8600", "#137333", "#d2e3fc", "#ceead6" ] } }, "yaxis": { "categoryorder": "total ascending", "tickfont": { "size": 21 }, "mirror": true, "ticks": "outside", "showline": true }, "xaxis": { "tickfont": { "size": 21 }, "title": { "text": "X-axis" }, "mirror": true, "ticks": "outside", "showline": true }, "margin": { "l": 300 }, "title": { "text": "X-Axis | 5Y
Date Ref: date_ref", "font": { "size": 24 } }, "font": { "size": 20 }, "autosize": false, "width": 2000, "height": 1000, "showlegend": true, "paper_bgcolor": "#fafafa", "plot_bgcolor": "#fafafa" } } ``` ### Steps To Reproduce _No response_ ### Expected Behavior ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/70647606/210408223-3967207e-a6fc-4d57-9e31-156c2a0fd03f.png) ### Current Behavior ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/70647606/210408192-0ed10297-46d5-4cad-b80b-86f70011f30f.png) ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: - Python version: - Operating System: - Browser: - Virtual environment: ### Additional Information https:///t/plotly-chart-displays-index-names-that-do-not-exists/35273 ### Are you willing to submit a PR? - [ ] Yes, I am willing to submit a PR!

Hi @participant3 @participant1 ,

I prepared a reproducible example for this issue, so you can clearly see the bug. See below.

Hope it can get fixed soon as it is confusing my app's users a lot. Still not experienced enough to submit PR but let me know if I can help in any other way. Thanks in advance!

```
import streamlit as st
from plotly.graph_objects import Figure, Scatter

st.title('Streamlit is incorrectly caching plotly data')

selected_dataset = st.selectbox(
    label = 'Switch between datasets to see incorrect plotly behavior',
    options = ['Single datapoint','Five datapoints']
    )

if selected_dataset == 'Single datapoint':
    x = [0]
    y = [17.3]
elif selected_dataset == 'Five datapoints':
    x = [0,2,4.5,10,13]
    y = [17.3,50,23.881,990,4]

fig = Figure(data=Scatter(x=x,y=y))
st.plotly_chart(fig)
```

Hi there @participant3 ,

I spent some time trying to identify the root cause, and this looks like a **regression starting from Streamlit version 1.15.0 onwards**. The reproducible example I posted earlier in this thread works correctly up until 1.14.1 (and for full context, this was tested using plotly 5.12.0).

In the changelog I saw that Streamlit 1.15.0 introduced some updates to how Streamlit handles plotly (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/5645), but maybe there were more changes that should be investigated?

Hope this helps.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Looks like this is in fact a regression on Plotly. We upgraded the version in our initial efforts which caused the issue. It was filed https://github.com/plotly/plotly.js/issues/6407 and fixed https://github.com/plotly/plotly.js/pull/6429. As a part of regularly upgrading our dependencies, we have successfully included 2.17.1. See [Changelog](https://github.com/plotly/plotly.js/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#2171----2023-01-09)

You can verify this by downloading our nightly `pip install streamlit-nightly`, and you can ensure this works. This will be included in the next release, 1.18.0. Thank you for your patience and thanks @participant3 for looking into it!

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
I'm also experiencing this issue on streamlit v `1.23:26` and the head of the `develop` branch when using `Scattermapbox` (`Scattergeo` is okay). This would lead me to believe the issue is with mapbox/plotly, however `fig.show()` in my code shows the correct plot and adding a `fig.show` within streamlit [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/7c92e092db361d5e66c409d7af1f59626292bfb1/lib/streamlit/elements/plotly_chart.py#L163) and a `pio.show` [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/7c92e092db361d5e66c409d7af1f59626292bfb1/lib/streamlit/elements/plotly_chart.py#L218) shows the correct figure - so streamlit is receiving the correct figure. EDIT: I have since tried this as a plotly dash app and that works fine, so I am quite confident this is a streamlit issue As my issue is `Scattermapbox` specific I'm not sure if it should be made a separate issue, that's up to you. Here is a minimal example - some of the code might look odd but it is there to accommodate additional functionality in my other work. [![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https:///badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https:///?issue=gh-5902) ```python import pandas as pd import plotly.graph_objects as go import numpy as np import streamlit as st # without a token you'll get an empty plot, they are free to get at mapbox.com mapbox_token = open(".mapbox_token").read() st.set_page_config(layout="wide") periods_dt = ["201604", "201605"] period = st.select_slider("Period",periods_dt,value=periods_dt[0]) period = pd.to_datetime(period, format="%Y%m") df_plot = pd.DataFrame( [ ['01/04/2016',1,2,1], ['01/05/2016',3,4,-2] ], columns=['t','i','j','v'] ) df_plot['t'] = pd.to_datetime(df_plot['t'], dayfirst=True) df_plot['q'] =0 df_plot = df_plot[df_plot['t']==period] def plotting_values(df, opacity_sorted, opacity, colours): lat_lons = { 1:{'geo_lon': -51, 'geo_lat': -14}, 2:{'geo_lon': 8, 'geo_lat': 9}, 3:{'geo_lon': 113, 'geo_lat': 0}, 4:{'geo_lon': 127, 'geo_lat': 35} } fig = go.Figure() lats = [] lons = [] hover_names = [] for style_idx,style in enumerate(opacity_sorted): for idx, row in df.loc[opacity[opacity==style].index].iterrows(): source = lat_lons[row['i']] target = lat_lons[row['j']] num_points = 100 lats.extend(np.linspace(source['geo_lat'], target['geo_lat'], num_points, endpoint=True)) lons.extend(np.linspace(source['geo_lon'], target['geo_lon'], num_points, endpoint=True)) lats.append(None) lons.append(None) t = f"""From {row['i']} to {row['j']}
""" hover_names.extend([t]*num_points) hover_names.append(None) # using Scattergeo makes it work fig.add_trace(go.Scattermapbox( mode = "lines", lon = lons, lat = lats, line = {'width': 2, 'color':[style_idx]}, hoverinfo = 'text', text = hover_names, opacity = 1, )) lats = [] lons = [] hover_names = [] return fig def create_plot(df, dt): # there's usually some logic behind the opacity vars, it doesn't affect the issue opacity_sorted = np.array([0.5, 1]) opacity = pd.Series(1.0, name='v') if dt.month==4 else pd.Series(0.5, name='v', index=[1]) colours = ['red', 'blue'] fig = plotting_values(df, opacity_sorted,opacity, colours) fig.update_layout(title=f"{dt}", showlegend=False, height=1000,hoverlabel_align='left', margin={"r":0,"l":0,"b":0, 't':30}) fig.update_mapboxes(zoom=1.9, accesstoken=mapbox_token) return fig _fig = create_plot(df_plot, period) _fig.show() st.plotly_chart(_fig, use_container_width=True) ``` using versions ``` numpy 1.25.2 pandas 2.0.3 plotly 5.15.0 streamlit 1.26.0 ```
